title: Instance.Name
summary: An instance's display name — NOT a unique ID. Siblings can share names, names can change at runtime; use FindFirstChild for lookups and don't key critical logic on names alone.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Readable name. Not guaranteed unique among siblings. Renamable at runtime (server authority for replicated instances).

explanation.whatItIs: The label on an object. Convenient for humans, treacherous as a program key.
explanation.whyItExists: Hierarchy navigation and display need names; uniqueness was never promised.
whenToUse: FindFirstChild lookups when you control the naming
whenNotToUse: As unique identifiers — players can rename characters; builders duplicate names
For security checks ('if tool.Name == "AdminSword"' — clients can rename)
tips: For uniqueness use tags, attributes, or object references
GetFullName() gives the dot-path for debugging
commonMistakes: Assuming name lookups are unique — FindFirstChild returns 'the first' found, whatever that is

examples.title: Name-based lookup with caveats
examples.code:
local chest = workspace:FindFirstChild("TreasureChest")
-- fine when YOU control naming…

-- …but never base security on names:
-- if tool.Name == "GoldenKey" then (client can rename!)
-- Instead: check an attribute/tag set by the server:
-- if tool:GetAttribute("IsGoldenKey") then
